method: Roll calls: for each bill, the official Kentucky LRC vote-history PDF (apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/<session>/<bill>/vote_history.pdf, which reprints the House RCS and Senate RSN roll-call sheets) was read with WebFetch (curl to the LRC host is blocked from the sandbox). Only passage, final-passage/concurrence and veto-override motions were kept (amendment, table, rules-suspension, previous-question and divide motions skipped). Bill descriptions and action histories (veto/override dates) come from the LRC bill pages (billPage). Bills were found from news coverage of the 2023-2026 sessions (veto-override roundups, Kentucky Lantern, WKYT/WVXU, Kentucky Right to Life) and then confirmed on the LRC site; every LRC page was read 2026-10-30. Each roll call's YEA/NAY/PASS-or-ABSTAIN/NOT-VOTING name lists were checked in code to equal the printed counts on the same sheet, and each chamber-year's union of names was checked for duplicates and completeness (100 House / 37-38 Senate labels; 2023 Senate had 37 seated, 2024 House HB 357/HB 2 sheets total 98, matching the printed counts). Caveat: the PDFs were transcribed by WebFetch's page reader, not by a local PDF parser; lists were reconstructed in print order and count-verified, but a swap of two names between columns would not be caught by counts alone. The HB 2 (2026) House passage sheet (RCS 170) needed one re-read by the reader; its lists verify but treat it as lower-confidence. Sheets print surnames only (e.g. 'Huff T', 'Lewis D', 'Bratcher S.', 'Frazier Gordon' in 2023-24 = 'Gordon' in 2025-26, 'Lewis' in 2025 = 'Lewis C' in 2026 = Chris Lewis). Candidates (_candidates.json) were matched to labels by chamber and session: 'Roberts' in 2023-24 is Rep. Rachel Roberts (D), so T.J. Roberts is matched only in 2025-26; Senate and House labels are matched only within their own chamber (e.g. Senate 'Nemes' = Mike Nemes, House 'Nemes' = Jason Nemes; Senate 'Smith' = Brandon Smith, House 'Smith' = Tom Smith). Same-surname challengers (Suhas Kulkarni, Pamela Lewis, David Johnson, Cherlyn Smith, Almaria/Joshua Baker, Stephanie White) are NOT matched. In members[].votes: 'Y'/'N' as printed; 'NV' = listed under PASSES (Senate), ABSTAINED or NOT VOTING on that sheet; a missing key = the person was not a member of that chamber on that sheet. incumbent=true means the candidate holds this same chamber+district on the current legislature.ky.gov House and Senate rosters (fetched 2026-10-30); sittingLegislator=true means a current member (all 106 sitting members on the ballot are running for their own seat). Killian Timoney (HD 45 challenger) is a former House member: incumbent/sitting false, but his 2023-24 House votes are included. conservativeSide is 'Y' for every roll call here (the bill sponsors' side). Values: marriage = gender policy for minors; limitedGov = union-dues payroll deduction, school-choice amendment, DEI ban, Medicaid work requirements; fiscal = income-tax cuts and Medicaid. LegiScan/Ballotpedia were not used.

notCaptured: proLife: no 2023, 2024 or 2026 House floor vote on an abortion bill was found. 2024 HB 467 (perinatal palliative care) never got a floor vote; 2026 HB 646 (abortion-pill trafficking) never left committee. 2026 SB 72 (conscience rights) passed the Senate only. HB 90 (2025) is the only House pro-life roll call; KRTL backed it, Planned Parenthood opposed it, and Republican Reps. Grossl and King also voted no (their reason was not found), so a no on HB 90 may not mean an anti-life position for those two.

marriage: 2026 bills (HB 553 gender-transition funding ban, HB 334 / SB 179 'Women's Bill of Rights', SB 184 Title IX oversight) got no floor votes. 2024 gender/family floor votes were not searched in depth.

religiousLiberty: 2025 SB 60 (RFRA strengthening) passed the Senate only; Ten Commandments bills (2025 HB 65, 2026 HB 670) never left committee. HB 547 (2023) passed both chambers per the vote sheets, but whether it became law was not checked. The House has only SB 19 (2025, two votes) and HB 547 (2023, one vote).
secondAmendment: no 2023 or 2025 gun floor vote was captured; 2023 'HB 153' was not checked.

fiscal: HB 1 (2025) is only weakly party-split (House 90-7, Senate 34-3). 2024 income-tax trigger legislation and the budget bills (2024 HB 6, 2026 HB 500 line-item overrides) were not captured. 2025 HB 6 (regulations) and 2026 HB 10 (limits on a governor's final-180-day actions) were seen in news but not fetched.

Procedural roll calls (motions to table, divide, previous question, suspend rules) were excluded, as were Senate passage votes of HB 2 (2026, RSN 4114/4133) where Democratic and Republican votes crossed.
Pre-2023 service: votes before the 2023 session were not collected (e.g. Johnny Ray Turner, a former state senator running in HD 95, has no 2023-26 record).

HB 90 and HB 495 (2025) House override sheets are labelled 'Final Passage' on 3/27/2025; the LRC action history for HB 495 (and HB 4) confirms that the House veto-override votes that day had the same counts (HB 495 78-20, HB 4 79-19, HB 90 77-20 by sheet).
